name: Barbell Bench Press
desc: The classic horizontal press for building chest, shoulder, and triceps strength.
steps: Lie flat with eyes under the bar, feet planted, and grip slightly wider than shoulders.
Unrack and lower the bar to mid-chest with elbows tucked about 45 degrees.
Press back up to lockout, keeping shoulder blades pinched and hips on the bench.

name: Incline Barbell Press
desc: A barbell press on an incline that shifts emphasis to the upper chest.
steps: Set the bench to 30-45 degrees and grip just wider than shoulders.
Lower the bar to the upper chest under control.
Drive back to lockout without flaring the elbows.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
desc: An upper-chest emphasis press with a longer range of motion than the barbell.
steps: Set the bench to 30-45 degrees and start with dumbbells at shoulder level.
Press up and slightly inward until arms are extended.
Lower under control until you feel a stretch across the upper chest.

name: Flat Dumbbell Press
desc: A bench press with independent arms for balanced chest development.
steps: Lie flat with a dumbbell at each shoulder.
Press both bells up until arms are extended over the chest.
Lower slowly to a deep, comfortable stretch.

name: Decline Barbell Press
desc: A decline-angle press that biases the lower chest fibers.
steps: Secure your legs and lie back on the decline bench.
Lower the bar to the lower chest line.
Press up and slightly back toward your eyes.

name: Decline Dumbbell Press
desc: The dumbbell version of the decline press with a freer pressing arc.
steps: Lie on a decline bench with dumbbells at the lower chest.
Press up until arms are extended.
Control the descent for a full stretch.

name: Cable Fly
desc: An isolation movement that keeps constant tension on the chest through the full arc.
steps: Set pulleys at chest height and step forward with a slight stagger.
With soft elbows, sweep the handles together in a hugging arc.
Squeeze at the midline, then let the cables pull your arms open slowly.

name: Incline Cable Fly
desc: A low-to-high cable fly that finishes the upper chest.
steps: Set pulleys low and stand centered with a slight forward lean.
Sweep the handles up and together to eye height.
Pause at the top, then lower on the same arc.

name: Dumbbell Fly
desc: A stretch-focused isolation for the pecs with light weight and strict form.
steps: Lie flat with dumbbells over the chest, palms facing.
Open your arms in a wide arc with soft elbows.
Stop at a deep stretch and squeeze back together.

name: Pec Deck
desc: A machine fly that locks the path so you can chase the squeeze.
steps: Adjust the seat so handles sit at chest height.
Bring the pads together in front of you.
Hold the squeeze, then open slowly to a stretch.

name: Machine Chest Press
desc: A guided pressing pattern that is easy to load and easy on the joints.
steps: Set the seat so handles line up with mid-chest.
Press to full extension without locking hard.
Return until your hands are just outside the chest.

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
desc: A fixed-path bench press for controlled heavy pressing without a spotter.
steps: Set the bench so the bar tracks to mid-chest.
Unhook, lower to the chest under control.
Press to lockout and re-hook safely.

name: Push-Up
desc: The foundational bodyweight press — chest, triceps, and core in one move.
steps: Set hands slightly wider than shoulders in a straight-line plank.
Lower your chest to just above the floor, elbows about 45 degrees.
Push back up without letting the hips sag or pike.

name: Weighted Push-Up
desc: A push-up loaded with a plate or vest once bodyweight gets easy.
steps: Have a partner place a plate on your upper back, or wear a vest.
Keep a rigid plank as you lower to the floor.
Press up powerfully without losing the plate position.

name: Deficit Push-Up
desc: Hands on raised blocks for extra range and a deeper chest stretch.
steps: Set hands on plates or handles a few inches off the floor.
Lower your chest below hand level for a deep stretch.
Press back to a full plank lockout.

name: Close-Grip Push-Up
desc: A narrow-hand push-up that shifts the work onto the triceps and inner chest.
steps: Place hands directly under the shoulders.
Lower with elbows brushing your ribs.
Press up to full extension.

name: Landmine Press
desc: An angled one-arm press that is friendly to cranky shoulders.
steps: Wedge a barbell in a landmine and hold the end at your shoulder.
Press up and forward along the bar's arc.
Lower slowly back to the shoulder and repeat.

name: Svend Press
desc: Pressing plates squeezed between the palms for a constant inner-chest squeeze.
steps: Squeeze one or two small plates flat between your palms at the chest.
Press straight out until arms are extended.
Keep crushing the plates as you pull them back in.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
desc: An arc from over the face to behind the head that stretches chest and lats together.
steps: Lie across a bench holding one dumbbell over your chest.
Lower it in an arc behind your head with soft elbows.
Pull it back over your chest without sitting up.

name: Deadlift
desc: The heaviest pull in the gym: total posterior chain, grip, and back strength.
steps: Stand with mid-foot under the bar; hinge and grip just outside your legs.
Brace, flatten your back, and push the floor away to stand tall.
Lock out with glutes, then hinge the bar back down under control.

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
desc: A neutral-handle deadlift that is easier on the lower back and simple to learn.
steps: Stand centered inside the trap bar and grip both handles.
Brace and stand tall, driving through the whole foot.
Set the bar down under control between reps.

name: Snatch-Grip Deadlift
desc: A wide-grip deadlift that hammers the upper back and grip.
steps: Take a very wide grip so the bar sits high on your thighs at lockout.
Keep the chest proud as you break the floor.
Stand tall, then lower with the same flat back.

name: Rack Pull
desc: A partial deadlift from the rack for overloading the top half of the pull.
steps: Set the pins just below knee height.
Grip, brace, and pull to a full standing lockout.
Return the bar to the pins without bouncing.

name: Barbell Row
desc: The staple bent-over pull for a thick, strong back.
steps: Hinge to about 45 degrees with the bar hanging at arm's length.
Row the bar to your lower ribs without standing up.
Lower slowly until arms are straight again.

name: Pendlay Row
desc: A strict row from a dead stop on the floor every rep.
steps: Set up parallel to the floor with the bar on the ground.
Explosively row the bar to the lower chest.
Return it fully to the floor and reset each rep.

name: Dumbbell Row
desc: A one-arm row with support that lets you pull heavy safely.
steps: Brace one hand and knee on a bench, back flat.
Row the dumbbell to your hip pocket.
Lower to a full stretch without rotating open.

name: Chest-Supported Row
desc: Rowing prone on an incline bench takes the lower back out of it entirely.
steps: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with dumbbells hanging.
Row both bells toward your hips.
Squeeze the shoulder blades, then lower slowly.

name: T-Bar Row
desc: A landmine-style row that lets you stack plates for back thickness.
steps: Straddle the bar and grip the handles under your chest.
Row the plates to your torso with elbows tight.
Lower under control without dropping your chest.

name: Meadows Row
desc: A one-arm landmine row with a big stretch at the bottom.
steps: Stand perpendicular to a landmine bar and grip the end.
Row the sleeve up toward your hip.
Let the weight pull into a deep stretch each rep.

name: Seal Row
desc: Rowing while lying flat on a high bench — zero momentum, all back.
steps: Lie prone on a high flat bench with the bar hanging below.
Row the bar to touch the bench underside.
Lower to a dead hang before the next rep.

name: Inverted Row
desc: A horizontal bodyweight pull — the push-up's mirror image.
steps: Hang under a bar with your body in a straight line.
Pull your chest to the bar, squeezing the blades.
Lower to straight arms without sagging hips.

name: Pull-Up
desc: The king of upper-body pulls: chin over the bar from a dead hang.
steps: Hang from an overhand grip just wider than shoulders.
Drive elbows down to pull your chin over the bar.
Lower all the way to a dead hang each rep.

name: Chin-Up
desc: An underhand pull-up with a stronger biceps contribution.
steps: Hang with palms facing you, shoulder-width apart.
Pull until your chin clears the bar.
Lower under control to full hang.

name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
desc: Palms-facing pull-up that most shoulders find the most comfortable.
steps: Grip parallel handles and start from a dead hang.
Pull your chest toward the handles.
Lower slowly with shoulders active.

name: Assisted Pull-Up
desc: Machine or band assistance on the way to your first strict pull-ups — more help means an easier rep.
steps: Kneel on the assist pad or loop a band under your feet.
Pull your chin over the bar with strict form.
Reduce the assistance over time as reps grow.

name: Lat Pulldown
desc: The cable version of a pull-up, loadable to the pound.
steps: Grip the bar wide and lock your thighs under the pads.
Pull the bar to your collarbone with a proud chest.
Let the bar rise until arms fully stretch.

name: Close-Grip Lat Pulldown
desc: A narrow neutral grip pulldown with a long stretch and strong lat line.
steps: Attach a close neutral handle and sit tall.
Pull the handle to your sternum.
Control the stretch at the top fully.

name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
desc: A unilateral pulldown to even out side-to-side lat strength.
steps: Grip one handle overhead, kneeling or seated.
Pull the elbow down to your side.
Resist the cable back to a full reach.

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
desc: A lat isolation with locked arms sweeping the bar to the thighs.
steps: Hold the bar at shoulder height, arms straight.
Sweep it down to your thighs in an arc.
Let it rise until you feel the lats stretch.

name: Cable Pullover
desc: A lying or standing cable arc that isolates the lats through a long range.
steps: Face away from a high pulley holding the rope overhead.
Pull the rope down and past your hips with straight arms.
Return overhead slowly, keeping ribs down.

name: Seated Cable Row
desc: A seated horizontal pull with constant cable tension for the mid-back.
steps: Sit tall with knees soft and grab the handle.
Row to your stomach, driving elbows back.
Reach forward slowly to stretch between reps.

name: Machine Row
desc: A supported machine pull that is simple to load and progress.
steps: Set the chest pad so arms fully extend at the start.
Row the handles to your torso.
Squeeze, then return to a full stretch.

name: Renegade Row
desc: Rowing from a plank — anti-rotation core work meets back training.
steps: Set a plank with hands on two dumbbells.
Row one bell to your hip without twisting.
Lower and alternate sides with square hips.

name: Barbell Back Squat
desc: The barbell squat: the cornerstone of lower-body strength.
steps: Bar on upper back, feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Sit down between your hips until thighs reach parallel or below.
Drive up through the whole foot, knees tracking the toes.

name: Front Squat
desc: A bar-in-front squat that keeps the torso tall and quads loaded.
steps: Rack the bar on your front delts with high elbows.
Squat deep while keeping the chest vertical.
Stand up without letting the elbows drop.

name: Box Squat
desc: Squatting to a box builds position, depth consistency, and starting power.
steps: Set a box at parallel height behind you.
Sit back until you touch the box under control.
Pause briefly, then drive up without rocking.

name: Pause Squat
desc: A squat with a dead stop in the hole to kill the bounce and build strength.
steps: Descend to your full depth.
Hold a strict two-to-three second pause without relaxing.
Drive up hard with no rebound.

name: Zercher Squat
desc: Bar cradled in the elbows — brutal for the core and upper back.
steps: Cradle the bar in the crook of your elbows.
Squat deep, keeping the bar tight to your body.
Stand tall while resisting the forward pull.

name: Goblet Squat
desc: A single-bell squat that teaches perfect squat posture.
steps: Hold a kettlebell at your chest with both hands.
Squat between your elbows to full depth.
Drive up tall without dropping the bell.

name: Smith Machine Squat
desc: A fixed-path squat useful for controlled overload and burnouts.
steps: Set your feet slightly ahead of the bar path.
Lower to parallel keeping the torso stable.
Press through the floor to full lockout.

name: Hack Squat
desc: A sled-guided squat that loads the quads without balancing a bar.
steps: Shoulders under the pads, feet mid-platform.
Lower until thighs pass parallel.
Drive up without slamming into lockout.

name: Leg Press
desc: Big leg loading with the back fully supported.
steps: Feet shoulder-width on the platform.
Lower the sled until knees near your chest.
Press through the whole foot without locking hard.

name: Leg Extension
desc: Pure quad isolation with a squeeze at the top.
steps: Line your knees up with the machine's pivot.
Extend to a straight leg and squeeze.
Lower slowly without letting the stack slam.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
desc: A rear-foot-elevated split squat — the great equalizer for legs.
steps: Place your rear foot on a bench behind you.
Lower straight down until the rear knee nears the floor.
Drive up through the front foot.

name: Split Squat
desc: A stationary lunge pattern for single-leg strength and balance.
steps: Take a long stride stance and stay tall.
Lower the back knee toward the floor.
Push through the front heel to stand.

name: Walking Lunge
desc: Alternating lunges that cover ground and torch the legs.
steps: Step forward into a deep lunge.
Drive through the front leg and step straight into the next.
Keep the torso tall the whole walk.

name: Reverse Lunge
desc: Stepping backward is easier on the knees and heavy on the glutes.
steps: Step one foot back into a lunge.
Lower the back knee to just above the floor.
Push through the front foot to return.

name: Curtsy Lunge
desc: A cross-behind lunge that finds the glute medius.
steps: Step one leg diagonally behind the other.
Lower until the front thigh is near parallel.
Drive back up and switch sides.

name: Step-Up
desc: Stepping onto a box with load — honest single-leg work.
steps: Place one whole foot on a knee-high box.
Drive through that leg to stand on top.
Lower slowly with the same leg doing the work.

name: Sissy Squat
desc: A knees-forward squat variation that isolates the quads intensely.
steps: Rise onto your toes and lean back from the knees.
Let the knees travel forward as you lower.
Squeeze the quads to return upright.

name: Pistol Squat
desc: A full single-leg squat to the floor — strength, mobility, and balance in one.
steps: Stand on one leg with the other held out front.
Squat all the way down under control.
Drive up without touching the free foot down.

name: Cyclist Squat
desc: Heels elevated, narrow stance — all knee travel, all quads.
steps: Stand with heels on a wedge or plates.
Squat deep letting the knees travel far forward.
Drive up staying tall through the torso.

name: Wall Sit
desc: An isometric hold at ninety degrees that burns out the quads.
steps: Slide down a wall until thighs are parallel.
Keep shins vertical and back flat on the wall.
Hold for time, breathing steadily.

name: Romanian Deadlift
desc: The hip hinge that builds hamstrings and glutes from a standing start.
steps: Hold the bar at your hips with soft knees.
Push your hips back until the hamstrings stretch hard.
Stand tall by squeezing the glutes through.

name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift
desc: A straighter-leg hinge from the floor for maximum hamstring stretch.
steps: Keep knees nearly straight as you hinge to the bar.
Grip and stand tall with a flat back.
Lower along your legs with hips high.

name: Single-Leg RDL
desc: A one-leg hinge that builds balance and hamstring control.
steps: Hinge forward on one leg, free leg trailing straight back.
Lower the weight toward the floor with square hips.
Squeeze the glute to return to standing.

name: Good Morning
desc: A barbell hinge with the bar on your back — potent posterior work.
steps: Set the bar as for squats and soften the knees.
Hinge until your torso nears parallel.
Drive the hips forward to stand.

name: Leg Curl
desc: Machine knee flexion to isolate the hamstrings.
steps: Line knees up with the pivot and hook your ankles.
Curl the pad toward your glutes.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.

name: Seated Leg Curl
desc: A seated curl that trains the hamstrings at a long muscle length.
steps: Sit with the pad locked over your thighs.
Curl your heels beneath the seat.
Return slowly against the stack.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
desc: Lowering your body from kneeling by hamstring strength alone.
steps: Anchor your ankles and kneel tall.
Lower your torso forward as slowly as possible.
Catch with your hands and push back lightly.

name: Glute-Ham Raise
desc: The GHD movement that curls your whole body up with hamstrings.
steps: Lock your feet in the GHD with knees on the pad.
Lower your torso toward horizontal.
Curl back to upright with hamstrings and glutes.

name: Sliding Leg Curl
desc: A bridge with sliders that curls the heels in and out.
steps: Bridge your hips up with heels on sliders.
Curl the heels toward your glutes.
Slide back out without dropping the hips.

name: Hip Thrust
desc: The barbell bridge that isolates and overloads the glutes.
steps: Upper back on a bench, bar over your hips.
Drive the hips to full lockout with a posterior tilt.
Lower a few inches and drive again.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
desc: A floor-based bridge for heavy, simple glute loading.
steps: Lie on the floor with the bar padded over your hips.
Drive hips up until your body forms a line.
Squeeze hard at the top, then lower.

name: Glute Bridge
desc: The bodyweight bridge — activation, burnouts, and beginners.
steps: Lie with knees bent, feet flat near your hips.
Squeeze the glutes to lift the hips.
Hold a beat at the top, then lower.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
desc: One-leg thrusts that expose and fix side-to-side gaps.
steps: Set up as a hip thrust with one foot down.
Drive that heel to full hip extension.
Keep the hips level the entire rep.

name: Frog Pump
desc: Soles-together pumps that flood the glutes with volume.
steps: Lie down, soles of feet pressed together, knees wide.
Drive the hips up through the outer feet.
Pump reps with a hard squeeze each time.

name: Sumo Deadlift
desc: A wide-stance pull that recruits more glutes and inner thigh.
steps: Take a wide stance, toes out, grip inside the knees.
Wedge hips down, chest up, and pull.
Lock out by driving the hips through.

name: Cable Pull-Through
desc: A cable hinge with the rope between your legs — glutes with backspin.
steps: Face away from a low pulley, rope between your legs.
Hinge forward letting the cable pull through.
Snap the hips forward to stand tall.

name: Cable Kickback
desc: A strict one-leg cable extension for the glute squeeze.
steps: Attach an ankle cuff and hinge slightly forward.
Kick the leg back and up without arching.
Return slowly, keeping tension on the glute.

name: Machine Hip Abduction
desc: Pressing the knees apart to build the glute medius.
steps: Sit with pads outside your knees.
Press your knees apart as far as possible.
Return slowly without letting the stack rest.

name: Banded Lateral Walk
desc: Side steps against a band to wake up the hips.
steps: Loop a band just above the knees and quarter-squat.
Step sideways keeping tension in the band.
Lead with the knee, not the foot, both directions.

name: Standing Calf Raise
desc: The straight-leg raise that builds the gastrocnemius.
steps: Balls of feet on the platform, heels hanging.
Drop into a deep stretch at the bottom.
Rise to your highest tiptoe and pause.

name: Seated Calf Raise
desc: A bent-knee raise that targets the deeper soleus.
steps: Sit with the pad over your knees, toes on the platform.
Lower heels to a full stretch.
Press up and squeeze at the top.

name: Donkey Calf Raise
desc: A hinged-over raise with a huge stretch on the calves.
steps: Hinge at the hips with toes on a block.
Sink the heels below the block.
Drive up onto the toes fully.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
desc: One-leg raises off a step — simple, brutal, effective.
steps: Stand on one foot on a step edge.
Lower the heel to a deep stretch.
Rise as high as possible onto the toe.

name: Leg Press Calf Raise
desc: Calf presses on the leg press sled for easy heavy loading.
steps: Place the balls of your feet on the platform's low edge.
Let the sled stretch your calves fully.
Press through the toes without bending knees.

name: Tibialis Raise
desc: Raising the toes against gravity to bulletproof the shins.
steps: Lean back against a wall, heels a foot out.
Lift your toes as high as they go.
Lower slowly and repeat for high reps.

name: Overhead Press
desc: The standing barbell press — raw shoulder strength, no backrest.
steps: Bar at your collarbones, grip just outside shoulders.
Brace and press straight up past your face.
Lock out overhead with biceps by your ears.

name: Push Press
desc: A leg-drive press that lets you overload the overhead lockout.
steps: Dip a few inches with a vertical torso.
Drive up with the legs and punch the bar overhead.
Lower to the shoulders under control.

name: Seated Dumbbell Press
desc: A supported dumbbell press for strict shoulder work.
steps: Sit tall with dumbbells at shoulder height.
Press up until the bells nearly touch overhead.
Lower to ear level under control.

name: Arnold Press
desc: A rotating press that sweeps the front and side delts.
steps: Start with palms facing you at the shoulders.
Rotate palms forward as you press overhead.
Reverse the rotation on the way down.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
desc: A guided press that keeps shoulders honest and safe under fatigue.
steps: Set the seat so handles start at shoulder height.
Press to full extension overhead.
Lower slowly without clanking the stack.

name: Landmine Shoulder Press
desc: An angled press that suits shoulders that hate strict vertical pressing.
steps: Hold the landmine end at one shoulder, staggered stance.
Press up and forward along the arc.
Control the return without shrugging.

name: Behind-the-Neck Press
desc: A behind-the-head press for mobile shoulders — light and strict.
steps: Grip wide with the bar behind your head.
Press straight up from the base of the neck.
Lower carefully only as far as mobility allows.

name: Lateral Raise
desc: The side-delt builder that gives shoulders their width.
steps: Stand tall with dumbbells at your sides.
Raise out to shoulder height, leading with the elbows.
Lower slowly — no swinging.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
desc: A cable side raise with tension from the very bottom.
steps: Stand beside a low pulley, handle in the far hand.
Raise the arm across and out to shoulder height.
Lower against the cable's pull slowly.

name: Single-Arm Cable Lateral
desc: Strict one-arm laterals for even shoulder caps.
steps: Grab the low pulley with your outside hand.
Raise to shoulder height without leaning.
Resist the negative all the way down.

name: Front Raise
desc: Raises to the front for the anterior delts.
steps: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Raise one or both to eye level.
Lower under control without swinging.

name: Plate Front Raise
desc: A single plate raised to eye level — simple front-delt finisher.
steps: Hold a plate at both sides like a steering wheel.
Raise it to eye level with straight-ish arms.
Lower slowly to the thighs.

name: Rear Delt Fly
desc: Bent-over reverse flys for the neglected rear delts.
steps: Hinge to near-parallel with dumbbells hanging.
Sweep the arms wide to shoulder height.
Lower slowly without standing up.

name: Face Pull
desc: A high rope pull to the face for rear delts and healthy shoulders.
steps: Set the rope at face height and grip thumbs-back.
Pull toward your eyes, elbows high and wide.
Finish with knuckles beside your ears.

name: Upright Row
desc: A vertical pull to the sternum for delts and traps.
steps: Grip the bar about shoulder width.
Pull to sternum height, elbows leading.
Lower under control; keep wrists relaxed.

name: Cuban Rotation
desc: An external-rotation press that armors the rotator cuff.
steps: Row light bells to an upright-row position.
Rotate the forearms up until vertical.
Press overhead, then reverse each step.

name: Pike Push-Up
desc: A hips-high push-up that presses like a handstand.
steps: Set a pike with hips high and hands ahead.
Lower the crown of your head to the floor.
Press back up along the same angle.

name: Handstand Push-Up
desc: The bodyweight overhead press — vertical pressing against the wall.
steps: Kick up to a wall handstand.
Lower your head to the floor under control.
Press back to a locked handstand.

name: Triceps Pushdown
desc: The staple cable extension for horseshoe triceps.
steps: Elbows pinned to your sides on a high pulley.
Push the bar down to full lockout.
Let it rise to a stretch without moving the elbows.

name: Rope Pushdown
desc: A rope pushdown with a spread at the bottom for a harder squeeze.
steps: Grip the rope with thumbs up, elbows tucked.
Push down and pull the rope apart at lockout.
Return slowly to a full stretch.

name: Skull Crusher
desc: Lying extensions to the forehead for mass on the long head.
steps: Lie back with the bar over your chest.
Bend only the elbows to lower toward your forehead.
Extend back to lockout without flaring.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
desc: A narrow-grip bench that turns the press into triceps work.
steps: Grip the bar just inside shoulder width.
Lower to the lower chest with tucked elbows.
Press up focusing on pushing with the triceps.

name: JM Press
desc: A hybrid of close-grip bench and skull crusher for pressing lockout.
steps: Lower the bar toward your chin, elbows tucked hard.
Let the forearms fold to about 45 degrees.
Extend back to lockout.

name: Overhead Cable Extension
desc: An overhead extension that stretches the long head under cable tension.
steps: Face away from the pulley with the rope overhead.
Extend to a full lockout in front of you.
Let the rope pull back to a deep stretch.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Extension
desc: A two-hand dumbbell extension from behind the head.
steps: Hold one bell overhead with both palms under the plate.
Lower it behind your head to a full stretch.
Extend to lockout keeping elbows narrow.

name: Triceps Kickback
desc: A strict rear extension with the upper arm frozen in place.
steps: Hinge over with the upper arm parallel to the floor.
Extend the forearm straight back to lockout.
Pause, then lower only the forearm.

name: Dip
desc: The bodyweight press for triceps and lower chest — add weight when ready.
steps: Support yourself on parallel bars, shoulders down.
Lower until upper arms reach parallel.
Press back to a straight-arm lockout.

name: Assisted Dip
desc: Machine-assisted dips on the way to full bodyweight — more help, easier rep.
steps: Kneel on the assist pad and grip the bars.
Lower to parallel upper arms.
Press up, trimming assistance as you get stronger.

name: Bench Dip
desc: Dips with hands on a bench — an anywhere triceps builder.
steps: Hands on a bench edge, legs extended forward.
Lower your hips until elbows hit ninety degrees.
Press back up without shrugging.

name: Diamond Push-Up
desc: Hands in a diamond — the hardest push-up for triceps.
steps: Form a diamond with thumbs and index fingers.
Lower your chest to your hands, elbows tight.
Press to lockout without flaring.

name: Tate Press
desc: Elbows-out dumbbell extensions to the chest for the lockout.
steps: Lie back with bells over your chest, palms forward.
Fold the elbows out so plates touch your chest.
Extend back up keeping bells together.

name: Barbell Curl
desc: The straight-bar curl — the biceps mass standard.
steps: Grip shoulder-width with elbows at your sides.
Curl to shoulder height without swinging.
Lower slowly to full extension.

name: EZ-Bar Curl
desc: An angled-grip curl that spares the wrists.
steps: Grip the angled sections at shoulder width.
Curl to the top with pinned elbows.
Control the negative fully.

name: Hammer Curl
desc: Neutral-grip curls that thicken the arm through the brachialis.
steps: Hold dumbbells with palms facing each other.
Curl without rotating the wrists.
Lower under control to your sides.

name: Cross-Body Hammer Curl
desc: Hammer curls across the torso for brachialis and forearm.
steps: Curl one bell across toward the opposite shoulder.
Keep the palm neutral the whole way.
Alternate arms with strict form.

name: Preacher Curl
desc: Curling over a pad removes all cheating from the equation.
steps: Armpits snug over the preacher pad.
Curl to the top without lifting the elbows.
Lower to a near-full stretch, no bouncing.

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
desc: Curling from a long stretch behind the body on an incline bench.
steps: Lie back on an incline with arms hanging.
Curl both bells without drifting the elbows forward.
Lower to a deep stretch behind you.

name: Concentration Curl
desc: The classic seated single-arm peak builder.
steps: Brace your elbow against your inner thigh.
Curl to your shoulder with zero swing.
Lower slow and full.

name: Spider Curl
desc: Chest-down curls with arms hanging vertical — pure peak contraction.
steps: Lie prone on an incline bench, arms hanging.
Curl the bells as high as possible.
Squeeze hard, then lower fully.

name: Cable Curl
desc: Curls with constant cable tension top to bottom.
steps: Grab a bar on the low pulley.
Curl to shoulder height with pinned elbows.
Resist the stack on the way down.

name: Bayesian Cable Curl
desc: A behind-the-body cable curl that loads the stretch hardest.
steps: Face away from a low pulley, arm trailing behind.
Curl forward and up to full contraction.
Let the cable pull back to a long stretch.

name: Zottman Curl
desc: Curl up palms-up, lower palms-down — biceps and forearms in one.
steps: Curl the bells with palms up.
Rotate to palms-down at the top.
Lower slowly in the reverse grip.

name: Drag Curl
desc: Dragging the bar up the torso with elbows sweeping back.
steps: Start a curl but pull the elbows behind you.
Drag the bar up your torso to the lower chest.
Lower along the same path.

name: Machine Curl
desc: A supported machine curl for clean, heavy contractions.
steps: Set the seat so elbows match the pivot.
Curl to full contraction.
Lower without letting the stack touch down.

name: Barbell 21s
desc: Seven bottom-half, seven top-half, seven full curls — one burning set.
steps: Do seven curls from bottom to halfway.
Do seven from halfway to the top.
Finish with seven full-range curls.

name: Wrist Curl
desc: Palms-up wrist flexion for forearm size and grip.
steps: Forearms on a bench, palms up, bar in fingers.
Curl the wrists up as high as possible.
Lower until the bar rolls to your fingertips.

name: Reverse Wrist Curl
desc: Palms-down wrist extension to balance the forearm.
steps: Forearms on a bench, palms down.
Raise the knuckles as high as possible.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.

name: Behind-the-Back Wrist Curl
desc: Standing wrist curls with the bar behind you — heavy and simple.
steps: Hold a bar behind your thighs, palms back.
Curl the wrists up, rolling to the fingers and back.
Keep arms still; only wrists move.

name: Reverse Curl
desc: An overhand curl that builds the brachioradialis ridge.
steps: Grip the bar palms-down at shoulder width.
Curl with pinned elbows and locked wrists.
Lower slowly to full extension.

name: Farmer's Carry
desc: Pick up heavy things and walk — grip, traps, and core in one.
steps: Deadlift a heavy bell in each hand.
Walk tall with tight ribs and level hips.
Carry for time or distance, then set down safely.

name: Plate Pinch
desc: Pinch-gripping smooth plates for crushing thumb strength.
steps: Pinch two plates smooth-side out between fingers and thumb.
Hold at your side for time.
Set them down before your grip fails.

name: Dead Hang
desc: Hanging from the bar for time — grip, shoulders, and spine decompression.
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip.
Keep shoulders slightly active, body still.
Hang for time and step off with control.

name: Towel Pull-Up
desc: Pull-ups gripping towels — savage grip with your back work.
steps: Drape two towels over the bar and grip them.
Pull your chin to hand height.
Lower under control without slipping.

name: Plank
desc: The isometric baseline for a braced, rigid torso.
steps: Forearms down, body in one straight line.
Squeeze glutes and brace like taking a punch.
Hold for time without sagging or piking.

name: Weighted Plank
desc: A plank with plates on your back once time gets long.
steps: Have a partner set a plate on your mid-back.
Hold a perfect line under the load.
End the set before form breaks.

name: Side Plank
desc: A lateral hold for the obliques and hip stability.
steps: Stack your feet with one forearm down.
Lift the hips into a straight side-on line.
Hold, then switch sides evenly.

name: Copenhagen Plank
desc: A side plank with the top leg on a bench — adductors of steel.
steps: Top foot on a bench, bottom leg free.
Lift into a side plank from the inner thigh.
Hold without letting the hips drop.

name: Hollow Body Hold
desc: The gymnast's dish hold that teaches total-body tension.
steps: Press your lower back into the floor.
Float arms and legs with ribs pulled down.
Hold the dish shape while breathing.

name: L-Sit
desc: Legs held at ninety on bars — compression strength for time.
steps: Support on parallettes or dip bars.
Lift straight legs to horizontal.
Hold with locked knees and tall shoulders.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
desc: Rolling out to a stretched plank and pulling back with pure abs.
steps: Kneel with the wheel under your shoulders.
Roll out as far as you can hold a flat line.
Pull back with abs, not hips.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
desc: Raising straight legs from a dead hang — the elite ab move.
steps: Hang with legs straight and together.
Raise your toes toward the bar without swinging.
Lower under control to a full hang.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
desc: The bent-knee version — the on-ramp to full leg raises.
steps: Hang from the bar, shoulders active.
Curl the knees to your chest.
Lower slowly without swinging.

name: Cable Crunch
desc: Kneeling crunches against the stack — abs you can load forever.
steps: Kneel below a high rope, hands by your head.
Crunch ribs to hips against the cable.
Return tall without pulling with your arms.

name: Sit-Up
desc: The classic full sit-up, strict and unanchored.
steps: Knees bent, feet flat, hands across chest.
Curl all the way up to your knees.
Lower one vertebra at a time.

name: V-Up
desc: Folding into a V — abs and hip flexors together.
steps: Lie flat with arms overhead.
Fold up, touching hands toward toes.
Lower both halves under control.

name: Russian Twist
desc: Seated rotations with a weight for the obliques.
steps: Sit back to a 45-degree lean, heels light.
Rotate the weight side to side.
Turn the shoulders, not just the arms.

name: Woodchopper
desc: A diagonal cable chop that trains rotation with load.
steps: Set the cable high and stand side-on.
Chop diagonally across to the opposite hip.
Control the return along the same line.

name: Pallof Press
desc: An anti-rotation press-out that the obliques hate quietly.
steps: Stand side-on holding the cable at your chest.
Press straight out and hold against the pull.
Return without letting your torso twist.

name: Dead Bug
desc: Opposite arm and leg reaches with the low back glued down.
steps: Lie down, arms up, knees over hips.
Extend opposite arm and leg to hover.
Return and switch without arching.

name: Bird Dog
desc: Opposite-limb reaches from all fours for a stable spine.
steps: From hands and knees, reach one arm and the opposite leg.
Hold a level pelvis for a beat.
Return quietly and switch sides.

name: Mountain Climbers
desc: Running knees in a plank — core work at conditioning pace.
steps: Set a strong high plank.
Drive knees toward your chest alternately.
Keep hips level and pace steady.

name: Dragon Flag
desc: The Bruce Lee move: lowering a rigid body from the shoulders.
steps: Grip the bench behind your head.
Raise your body to vertical on your shoulders.
Lower dead straight as slowly as possible.

name: Kettlebell Swing
desc: The ballistic hinge — power, posterior chain, and conditioning.
steps: Hike the bell back between your legs.
Snap the hips to float it to chest height.
Let it fall and hinge straight into the next rep.

name: Treadmill Run
desc: Steady-state or interval running, measured to the meter.
steps: Set your pace and incline.
Run tall with a quick, quiet cadence.
Cool down before stepping off.

name: Incline Treadmill Walk
desc: A steep walk that builds engine without pounding the joints.
steps: Set a steep incline and moderate speed.
Walk without holding the rails.
Keep a pace you could just hold a conversation at.

name: Rowing Erg
desc: The full-body engine builder: legs, back, and lungs.
steps: Drive with the legs first, then swing and pull.
Return hands-body-legs in that order.
Hold consistent split times.

name: Ski Erg
desc: A double-pole pull-down machine for lats and lungs.
steps: Reach tall and drive the handles down past your hips.
Hinge slightly with each pull.
Rise and repeat in rhythm.

name: Assault Bike
desc: The fan bike that punishes arms and legs together.
steps: Set your seat height and grab the handles.
Drive legs and arms together.
Hold pace or sprint in intervals.

name: Stationary Bike
desc: Low-impact cycling for steady aerobic work.
steps: Set saddle height so knees stay soft at the bottom.
Pedal at a steady cadence.
Add resistance for intervals.

name: Elliptical
desc: A smooth full-body glide for joint-friendly cardio.
steps: Step on and find a natural stride.
Push and pull the handles as you stride.
Keep effort even for the duration.

name: Stair Climber
desc: Endless stairs for legs and lungs.
steps: Step with your whole foot each stair.
Stand tall; fingertips only on the rails.
Climb at a sustainable pace.

name: Sled Push
desc: Driving a loaded sled — pure leg power with zero eccentric.
steps: Grip the poles low with a long spine.
Drive the sled with powerful steps.
Push for distance, rest, repeat.

name: Battle Ropes
desc: Violent rope waves for shoulders and conditioning.
steps: Athletic stance, one rope end per hand.
Whip alternating or double waves.
Keep the waves tall for the whole interval.

name: Jump Rope
desc: Skipping for footwork, calves, and cheap conditioning.
steps: Elbows in, wrists doing the turning.
Bounce low on the balls of your feet.
Build up time or add double-unders.

name: Burpees
desc: Floor to jump in one move — the conditioning tax collector.
steps: Drop through a push-up to the floor.
Snap your feet under you.
Jump tall with hands overhead.

name: Swimming Laps
desc: Full-body, zero-impact endurance in the pool.
steps: Pick a stroke and a target distance.
Swim controlled lengths with steady breathing.
Rest briefly at the wall between sets.
